metadata.note: The Pemigewasset Valley Railroad (chartered 1874) ran Plymouth - North Woodstock, NH (opened 1883) and was extended about a mile to Lincoln (1894, 1895 or 1896 - sources conflict; 1896 drawn). Known on the B&M as the Pemigewasset Valley Branch. The PV was a lessor company that never ran its own trains beyond, at most, one month in 1883, so it has no feature of its own: the branch is drawn as one feature per operator era (Rule 4), all on the same traced track - Boston, Concord & Montreal 1883-1884, Boston & Lowell 1884-1887, Boston and Maine 1887-1888, Concord & Montreal 1889-1895, and Boston and Maine from the 29 Jun 1895 lease (to North Woodstock 1895-1896, to Lincoln 1896-1951 [OPEN]). 1888-1889, when the B&L/B&M lease was vacated and the BC&M regained the road before the Sept 1889 Concord & Montreal merger, is left undrawn because the date possession returned is not established. Replaces feature bcm-pemigewasset-valley-plymouth-lincoln formerly in boston_concord_montreal_railroad.geojson, which drew the whole line 1883-1965 in a lessor colour on the Lincoln alignment.
sources: Official Guide of the Railways, Feb 1952 issue (schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951), Boston and Maine Table 21 “Pemigewasset Valley Branch” (research/sources/official_guide_1952.txt, OCR lines ~25575-25593)
geometry_sources: OpenStreetMap via Overpass (maps.mail.ru mirror), traced with opstrace.py. The branch is still in place (state-owned, operated by the Plymouth & Lincoln Railroad / Granite State Scenic Railway) and is tagged railway=rail name='Granite State Railway' old_railway_operator=B&M in OSM; the whole trace ran on B&M-tagged ways (opstrace: 21.2 mi 'B&M', 0 mi on any other operator, no straight legs, no spurs). Simplified with douglas_peucker(8 m) then trim_reversals. Waypoints: Plymouth station (hand-pinned on the track at Railroad Square, 43.7575 N; Nominatim's 'Plymouth, New Hampshire' is the township centroid 3 km SW, which the previous feature wrongly started from), Livermore Falls (Nominatim waterfall node, 0.1 km from line), West Campton (hamlet node, 1.5 km from line - the village sits west of the river; used only as a routing hint), West Thornton (hamlet node, 0.4 km), Lincoln station (hand-pinned on the OSM Lincoln station node). The line leaves Plymouth station northward on the shared track and diverges from the abandoned BC&M main line to Woodsville (which turns west at ~43.765 N) about 0.5 mi north of the station; it does not run onto the main line.
metadata.not_yet_sourced: END OF REGULAR PASSENGER SERVICE on the branch is [OPEN]: pv-bm-plymouth-lincoln is drawn to 1951, the last confirmed year (mixed train in the Feb 1952 Official Guide, schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951); no source found dates the last train (true end 1951-1965). Best next sources: a B&M public timetable 1953-1958, a 'last train to Lincoln' newspaper story, or ICC / NH PUC discontinuance filings. Also unresolved: the Lincoln extension year (1894 / 1895 / 1896 - 1896 drawn; sighting the 14 Jul 1894 C&M folder could move it to 1894 under the C&M); the date the BC&M regained the road from the B&L/B&M lease (1888 decision vs Sept 1889 merger; 1888-1889 undrawn); whether the PV sublease passed with the 1884 BC&M lease (inferred from Stearns); which OG52 Table 21 time column is the mixed train; all headways.
metadata.omitted: Not drawn here, deliberately: (1) the Hobo Railroad / Plymouth & Lincoln Railroad (Granite State Scenic Railway from 2024) tourist excursions, Lincoln - Woodstock area, 1987-present - a different operating company, to be added as its own layer; (2) Mass Bay RRE charter specials over the whole branch, single days in 2006 and 2022 [ANCHOR]; (3) the East Branch & Lincoln logging railroad (1893-1948), freight-only (Rule 1); (4) post-passenger freight to the Lincoln paper mill and later state-owned freight operation (Rule 1); (5) the 1975/76 Wolfeboro RR 'resumed service', not shown to be passenger service on this branch.

properties.geometry_quality: Plymouth - North Woodstock: traced 20.5 mi, cut where the line passes closest to North Woodstock village (44.0318 N, 0.5 km east of the village centre; the depot site itself was not separately located). Documented: 20.6 mi (Fowler, B&M line 29 mileposts 0.0-20.6), 'twenty miles' (Stearns 1906), 21 mi (Wikipedia). Caswell gives 22.93 mi for the whole road, which the earlier feature quoted as Plymouth - North Woodstock; Caswell's figure is for the line to Lincoln, and the trace is ~7% short of it even to Lincoln - it probably counts yard/mill track at Lincoln. No straight-line legs. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the track as it survives today (rebuilt over a century of B&M and state ownership); 1880s-1890s alignment differences are not drawn. The first ~0.5 mi out of Plymouth is the shared BC&M main-line track to the branch junction, which branch trains used from Plymouth station.

segments.note: The Pemigewasset Valley Railroad (chartered 1874) opened Plymouth - North Woodstock in 1883 (Stearns: 'completed ... in 1883'; Caswell: 'the road was opened in 1883'). The PV was a lessor company: Stearns says 'from the beginning the road has been operated under a lease to the Boston, Concord, and Montreal'; Caswell gives a 99-year lease from 1883 at 6% on cost; Wikipedia has the PV company running it itself only 1 Mar - 1 Apr 1883, below the map's year resolution. Ends 1884 because the BC&M was leased to the Boston & Lowell on 1 Jun 1884 (Stearns) - an operator change, not a break in service. Line ends at North Woodstock; the Lincoln extension came 1894-1896. Headway is an estimate, not from any timetable (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: Stearns, History of Plymouth NH vol. I (1906), railroad chapter, for the 1883 opening, the BC&M lease from the beginning and the 1 Jun 1884 Boston & Lowell lease; Caswell for the 1883 opening and lease terms; Wikipedia for the one-month independent operation. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: On 1 Jun 1884 the Boston, Concord & Montreal was leased to the Boston & Lowell for 99 years and became its Northern Division (Stearns). That the Pemigewasset Valley sublease passed with it is INFERRED, not stated: Stearns says the PV was always worked under its BC&M lease, so whoever operated the BC&M ran PV trains. Ends 1887 when the Boston and Maine leased the Boston & Lowell (Wikipedia, Concord and Montreal Railroad) - an operator change, not a break. Headway is an estimate (Rule 3).

segments.note: Boston and Maine operation via its 1887 lease of the Boston & Lowell, which held the BC&M (and with it the PV) since 1884. Stearns: the BC&M 'was operated by the Boston and Maine until the lease was vacated' by legal process; the BC&M won its action to recover the road on forfeiture grounds in Boston, C. & M. R. v. Boston & Lowell, 65 N.H. 393 (1888). The date possession returned (1888 decision vs the Sept 1889 Concord & Montreal merger) is not pinned, so this era is drawn only to 1888, the earlier end, and 1888-1889 is left undrawn rather than assigned a guessed operator. Headway is an estimate (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: Stearns (1906) for B&M operation until the lease was vacated; 65 N.H. 393 (1888) for the forfeiture judgment; Wikipedia 'Concord and Montreal Railroad' for the 1887 B&M lease of the B&L. Headway not sourced.

segments.note: The Boston and Maine leased the Concord & Montreal on 29 Jun 1895 (Stearns) and took over the branch. Drawn to North Woodstock only for 1895-1896 because the North Woodstock - Lincoln extension year is in conflict: 1894 (a C&M public folder corrected to 14 Jul 1894 lists Lincoln, seen only in the Nashua City Station transcription), 1895 (Caswell) or 1896 (Stearns: 'In 1896 the track was extended about three miles to a point in Lincoln'). The latest date, 1896, is drawn so the extension is never claimed before it is confirmed. From 1896 see pv-bm-plymouth-lincoln. Headway is an estimate (Rule 3).
sources: Segment-level: Stearns (1906) for the 29 Jun 1895 B&M lease and the 1896 extension year; Caswell (1895) and Nashua City Station (1894 folder) for the conflicting extension years. Headway not sourced.

Headway is an estimate (Rule 3).

The North Woodstock - Lincoln extension is 0.7 mi of the trace against 1.0 mi in Fowler (20.6 to 21.6) and 'about three miles' in Stearns (probably to J. E. Henry's mill yard). No straight-line legs. ERA CAVEAT: drawn on the present-day track (ex-B&M, state-owned since 1975/76, used by the Hobo / Granite State Scenic tourist trains); earlier alignment and yard-layout differences at Plymouth and Lincoln are not drawn. The first ~0.5 mi out of Plymouth is shared main-line track to the junction.

segments.note: Boston and Maine Pemigewasset Valley Branch, Plymouth - North Woodstock - Lincoln, after the extension to Lincoln (J. E. Henry's mill town and junction with his East Branch & Lincoln logging railroad, which was freight-only and is not drawn). Operated by the B&M under its 29 Jun 1895 lease of the Concord & Montreal; the 1919 formal merger changed no operator. Start 1896 is the latest of three conflicting extension dates (1894 NCS folder, 1895 Caswell, 1896 Stearns) - the confirmed one. END IS [OPEN]: a mixed train with times is in the Feb 1952 Official Guide, B&M Table 21 'Pemigewasset Valley Branch' (schedules eff. 30 Sep 1951), alongside motor coaches. 1951 is the last CONFIRMED year of passenger service, NOT a known end - no source found dates when service actually stopped (the true end lies somewhere 1951-1965: it cannot have outlasted Concord - Plymouth passenger service). Do not extend without evidence. B&M employee timetables of 1963 and 1967 listing Lincoln are operating documents that include freight stations and do not prove passenger service. Headway is an estimate (Rule 3); by 1951 the OCR suggests a single mixed train each way.
sources: Segment-level: Stearns (1906) for the B&M lease and 1896 extension; Official Guide Feb 1952 B&M Table 21 for the Sept 1951 mixed train (the last confirmed year); Fowler and the Official Guide for mileage. Headway not sourced.
